StudentRecord.title: StudentRecord
StudentRecord.description: The authoritative student record held by an institute. ONE schema is shared by all three institutes, which is the point of the multi-tenant demo rather than an economy: Horizonte, Atlantico and Aurora hold structurally identical records and are kept apart by osTenantId alone, so an isolation failure shows up as one institute reading another's rows rather than as a schema mismatch that would have masked it. studentId is unique WITHIN a tenant, never across the platform -- two institutes may legitimately both number a student 2026-0001.

studentId.title: Student ID
studentId.description: The institute's own roll number, e.g. HOR-2026-0001. Unique within the issuing institute's tenant and meaningless outside it. Issuer-side only: it is never a credential claim, so a verifier cannot learn which institute's roll a student sat on.

nationalId.title: National ID
nationalId.description: Issuer-side lookup only, e.g. NAT-70011234. Matched against the authenticated account's nationalId claim to decide whose credential may be issued. NEVER issued as a credential claim and never disclosed to a verifier.

fullName.title: Full name
fullName.description: The student's name as the institute records it. Disclosable.

programme.title: Programme
programme.description: The course of study, e.g. Engenharia de Computacao. Free text rather than an enum: the three institutes teach different programmes, and constraining them to a shared vocabulary would be a modelling claim this demo does not need to make.

enrolmentStatus.title: Enrolment status
enrolmentStatus.description: Controlled vocabulary. Only COMPLETED and ENROLLED describe a student in good standing; the rest exist so that a genuine, fully verified credential can still produce a negative answer.

percentage.title: Percentage
percentage.description: Marks percentage, 0 through 100. Compared against thresholds with integer arithmetic so a boundary is exact: 60 must pass a >=60 rule and 59.99 must not, regardless of how the value survives JSON. A value with finer precision than the schema permits is MALFORMED, not a business answer.
